messages: Create a bilingual (English and Chinese) landing page for "Repro Desk", a service that checks whether a research paper's headline number can be reproduced. Include a hero, three steps, a sample report card, a pricing section with free pilot plans, an FAQ, and a request form (paper link, claim, email) that saves to the database. Add an admin page, behind login, that lists the requests.
I'm setting up the full-stack template with the Atoms Cloud backend, since the request form and admin login both need it.
Next I'll read the backend and frontend READMEs so the build follows the template's APIs.
Now I'll read the required Web SDK guide and check the existing tables.
No relevant tables exist yet, so I'll create the `repro_requests` table now.
I'll check the generated router to see whether anonymous visitors can submit without logging in.
I'll read the generated router's list and create endpoints to see how they handle auth.
Those generated endpoints let anyone read the table, so I'll find the auth dependency I can use to lock down the listing endpoints.
I'll replace the generated router with a locked-down version: anyone can submit a request, but only an admin can list them.
The admin role is assigned to the project owner, so only the owner can list requests; next I'll check the Python syntax and the frontend files I need to edit.
Backend is ready, so next I'll install GSAP, read the image-generation skill, and write the design spec.
I'm starting the three photo generations in the background and will write the frontend code while they run.
While the images generate, I'll write the theme, the bilingual content, the landing page, the admin page and the routes.
The images are done, so I'll read the results to get their URLs.
Images are ready; next I'll write the landing page, request form, admin page and routes.
Everything is written, so next I'll run lint and the production build.
Lint and build both pass, so next I'll fill in the empty architecture notes and run the visual check.
The check passed, but it noted the sections below the hero looked empty. That happens because the scroll reveals start content fully hidden, so I'll change them to keep content visible by default.

Repro Desk is built: a bilingual landing page and a login-protected admin page. Lint and the production build pass. A visual check found that the sections below the hero showed up empty, because scroll animations started them fully invisible. I changed the animations so the content is always readable, and lint and build pass again. I haven't re-run the visual check since that fix, and I haven't tested a real form submission or the admin login.

**Landing page**
- An EN / 中文 switch in the header changes all copy. The page also starts in Chinese if the visitor's browser is set to Chinese, and remembers the last choice.
- Sections: hero, three steps, a sample report card, pricing, FAQ (six questions), and the request form. Pricing has two free pilot plans, single-claim and lab, plus a custom ongoing plan.
- Choosing a plan scrolls to the form with that plan already selected.
- The form takes a paper link, the claim and an email. It checks each field before sending, saves the request to the database and shows a request number like RQ-0001.

**Admin page (`/admin`)**
- Visitors who aren't logged in see a login button.
- After login it lists all requests, newest first, with a status filter, paging, and a status menu on each row (new, in review, done, declined).
- Only the project owner's account can see the list. The server enforces this, so other logged-in accounts get a "no access" message and the data can't be read through the API either.
- A "Team login" link in the footer leads there.

The sample report and the hero's verdict badge use made-up example numbers, and the three photos are AI-generated.

You can preview it in App Viewer. Use the publish button to deploy it and share the link. If anything behaves unexpectedly, let me know.
